disease_label_per_paper: Heat stroke with rhabdomyolysis, acute kidney injury, progressive cerebral edema, and death
presentation_summary: 53-year-old woman was admitted with 2 days of altered mental status after being found unconscious and sweating at home.
She had alcohol abuse history; several empty alcohol bottles were found nearby. During the prior two days, highest environmental temperature was 36.0 C.
She had been externally cooled at home for about 14 hours with an air conditioner before hospital arrival, so arrival temperature was 38.0 C.
On arrival BP was 170/99 mmHg, pulse 137/min, and she was stuporous and responsive only to painful stimuli.
Labs showed CK 9676 U/L, creatinine 4.05 mg/dL, and BUN 86.6 mg/dL, indicating rhabdomyolysis and AKI.
Brain imaging showed cortical/deep gray diffusion restriction and rapidly progressive cerebral edema; she developed fixed dilated pupil, was intubated/ventilated, and died 11 days later.

imaging: Brain CT on admission showed multifocal low-density areas in bilateral hippocampi and left cerebral cortex.
MRI 5 hours after admission showed restricted diffusion in cerebral cortex, bilateral hippocampi, and basal ganglia with no significant white matter abnormality.
Follow-up CT one day later showed rapid progression of cerebral edema.
actual_treatment: intubation and mechanical ventilation after neurologic deterioration
quality_warnings: Arrival body temperature was only 38.0 C because the patient had already undergone prolonged home cooling; ranking evidence therefore preserves environmental heat exposure, delayed/low-intensity cooling context, CNS dysfunction, rhabdomyolysis, and AKI.
